paper1_fig1_design: Figure 1 | Separating acquisition, generalisation and benchmark validity. a, Retrospective replay reveals measurements after selection and refits a gradient-boosted learner. The reported permeability replay nevertheless uses full-source label statistics for normalisation; it is not a demonstrated causal, revealed-label-only normalisation experiment. b, Acquisition yield, held-out ranking and benchmark validity answer different questions and are assessed with separate controls. This is a protocol schematic, not an experimental result.
paper1_fig2_feedback: Figure 2 | Seed replication does not establish cross-source yield gain. Regime L, full-protocol replay, 10 seeds per learner. a, Loop-minus-frozen yield with 95% t intervals across seeds (blue) or source clusters (orange; 14 aware and 16 blind). b, Descriptive omission of the largest contributing source: 2020_Townsend for the aware learner (88.7% of absolute source contributions), 2021_Kelly for the blind learner (53.7%). Shares divide the absolute contribution of that source by the sum of absolute source contributions. Omission subtracts the observed contribution; it is not a rerun without that source. Omission points have no plotted uncertainty and are not independent tests. c, Full-pool loop-minus-frozen change in held-out within-source Spearman correlation, with 95% t intervals across 11 evaluable sources. Yield is measured in the acquisition pool; ranking is evaluated separately. All plotted values are read from the frozen source-cluster summary.
paper1_fig3_gate: Figure 3 | Calibration reduces false alarms and identifies the basis of the real-benchmark verdict. a, Registered and calibrated rules are evaluated on the same planted-valid null benchmarks (permuted real benchmark structures and synthetic family structures) within each displayed design (200 replicates at 14 families; 400 otherwise). Bars are 95% binomial intervals from the stored calibration evaluation. These matched comparison rates differ from the earlier, independent gate-positive-control experiment. Acceptance also requires an upper 95% bound no greater than 15%; it does not establish a population rate below 10%. The 14-family setting remains too weak to establish certification despite reduced false alarms. b, Absolute null-standardised statistics for selected analysis-I controls; dashed line is the calibrated critical value. Orange bars exceed the threshold: censoring, the Ki/Kd assay indicator and oxygen fraction. No primary compound-only control exceeds it. A gate verdict is not evidence of a model advantage.
paper1_fig4_transfer: Figure 4 | Few-label transfer remains unresolved beyond strong lookup controls. Exact-potency benchmark, test half: 86 targets in 21 families, equal weight per family. a, Descriptive hard-stratum learning curves; uncertainty is omitted from this panel for readability. b, Registered screening contrasts against the best baseline on the test half, with 97.5% family-cluster intervals at k=3,5,10. All six intervals include zero. These underpowered screening results do not establish equivalence or absence of benefit; they are distinct from the censoring-biased analysis-I classification benchmark.
